segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Hey Dana, yeah, thanks for making time. I wanted to check the final seat count before we send the revised order form. I have 84 full users and 19 read-only, with the support add-on for the finance team.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That's right. We may add three more full users in July, but don't hold the order for that. The bigger thing is the May timeline.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, I have services starting May 1 and a target go-live of May 15 for the first two workflows, then the reporting pack after Memorial Day.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, good. On the kickoff invite yesterday, your onboarding lead said May 22, so I just wanted to make sure we weren't already sliding a week.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Ah, sorry about that. I'll update the project notes after this and have her resend the milestone plan with May 15. The scope is still the same: intake, approvals, and the export to your accounting file.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Also, we got the invoice this morning for the full $46,800 upfront. The order form we reviewed had quarterly billing, net 30, starting on signature.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, I see quarterly on my pricing sheet. I'll have the billing team void that one and issue the first $11,700 invoice. You shouldn't need to route the annual amount.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Appreciate it. Legal is fine with the 24-month term and the standard auto-renew language, as long as we get the 60-day notice window in the notice section.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: That's in there. I'll send the clean version by 2 p.m. Eastern today, and if you can sign by Friday, we can keep the May 1 services start.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Works for me. Send it over, and I'll push it through procurement this afternoon.
